why: Most commands are sound. `npm test` maps to `node --test` in package.json, `git status` runs fine, and verifier Checks 1, 2 and 4 use valid quoting and valid ESM import code. Check 3 breaks. Its JS sits inside a bash double-quoted string, which turns `'\\b'` into `'\b'`. To JavaScript, `'\b'` in a string is a backspace character, not a word boundary. So `new RegExp('\b' + f + '\b')` looks for backspace characters, never matches a README heading, and every export is printed as missing. The check would FAIL even on a correct PR, so this command does not run as intended as written. (`'\n'` survives unchanged and works, but the `\\b` escaping is wrong.)
